transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-08-17 15:00 UTC | Duration: 57m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Alice Park (Redwood AE), Jonas Li (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Crestline PM), Tom Reyes (Eng), Priya Nair (InfoSec)

Summary: quick hosted API walkthrough focusing on chat and generation basics — streaming behavior, parameter impacts (temp/top_p/max_tokens), retry/backoff strategies, and what to expect re: latency vs cost. Customer cares about PII handling, SOC2, and whether hosted can meet 95th percentile latency SLA for triage flows.

Topics: onboarding, streaming chunks, backoff, idempotency, console traces, Optimize suggestions

[00:00] Alice: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. I'm Alice from Redwood, AE, and with me is Jonas our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maya: Good, thanks. Excited — we want to see how hosted would handle chat triage in our app.
[00:14] Tom: Quick note — I'm mainly here for performance questions and latency numbers.
[00:19] Jonas: Great, we'll start with a short agenda; demo the hosted chat endpoint, show streaming, then dig into params and retry patterns, then Q&A. We also have a sandbox key to hand off if you'd like.
[00:35] Maya: Timeline — we're aiming for a pilot by end of Sept, decision early Oct. Stakeholders are product, platform, and InfoSec.
[00:44] Priya: And compliance is the big one for us, SOC2, KMS for keys, and logs/audit retention.
[01:02] Alice: Noted. On the hosted side we support TLS, customer-managed KMS for private, and we can provide SOC2 docs. We'll put that in the follow-up pack.
[01:17] Jonas: Ok live demo — console up. I'm hitting the /v1/chat/completions endpoint — example payload: messages, model, stream: true, temperature: 0.2, top_p: 0.9, max_tokens: 128, stop: ["\n\n"]. I'll enable SSE stream in the browser so you can see partial tokens.
[01:40] [01:40] Jonas (typing): Starting stream — you'll see token chunks arrive roughly every 50-80ms depending on tokenization and model.
[01:51] [01:51] System: stream chunk: "Hi there, I'm an assistant..."
[02:05] Tom: Those chunk intervals look good; what's the 95th percentile on this model in our region?
[02:11] Jonas: For the m-3.6b quantized variant in us-west-2 we see median ~120ms per first token, 95th ~420ms for first token at current global load. We'll send benchmark spreadsheet — numbers vary with sequence length and batching.
[02:34] Maya: Can we tune temperature to make output more deterministic for triage categorization?
[02:40] Jonas: Yes — temperature 0-0.3 is common for deterministic. We also suggest setting top_k=40 or top_p 0.7 for constrained diversity. For classification-like outputs, you can use logit_bias and few-shot prompts.
[03:05] Jonas: Also, prefix caching/K V cache will help with follow-up context. Note sometimes transcriber shows K V cache as "K V" or "KV", sorry.
[03:20] Priya: On retries — how should our frontend handle transient errors? We need idempotency for user messages.
[03:27] Alice: Good question. For single-turn chat we recommend client-side idempotency keys on create to avoid double consumption of tokens. For streaming we support reconnections with resume tokens for short-lived disconnects.
[03:45] Jonas: Example pattern: implement exponential backoff with jitter, limit retries to 3 for 5xx or 429, and fall back to a smaller model or cached response if available. We'll put code snippets in the repo.
[04:05] [04:05] Maya: Can the stream reconnect mid-generation to resume where it left off?
[04:10] Jonas: We have a resume token pattern — but caveat: resume across different model variants or after KV cache eviction may not be exact. Best practice: small client-side buffer to replay last N tokens if reconnect.
[04:30] Tom: How about cost tradeoffs — what's the token accounting with streaming vs non-streaming?
[04:36] Jonas: Same token accounting; streaming is just delivery mode. Cost is model-dependent and per-token. But lower temperature or shorter max_tokens reduces cost. Also batching multiple user messages server-side helps amortize overhead.
[05:02] Maya: We want a fallback plan if hosted has a degradation window — can Redwood automatically route to a cheaper quantized model or to our dedicated pool?
[05:11] Alice: Yes — smart routing policies can fail over by policy: model-variant fallback, region fallback, or dedicated-as-fallback if you've purchased dedicated. We can set automatic thresholds to switch.
[05:28] Priya: Data retention — does hosted store prompts? We require customer data not to be used for training.
[05:35] Alice: Hosted by default keeps logs for X days for troubleshooting; enterprise contracts can set retention or opt-out of using data for model training. We'll include the privacy policy and an option for data isolation.
[05:58] Jonas: Now showing console traces — you can see per-request latency, token breakdown, and which kernel/instance served the request. We expose per-route dashboards and token-level cost estimates.
[06:20] [06:20] System: slide: "Retry strategy" — shows backoff params, idempotency keys, fallback steps.
[06:33] Maya: Sounds good. For our engineers, can we get a script that runs load with our prompt set so we can see p95 in our region?
[06:40] Jonas: Yes, we'll provide a small k6 + cURL harness tied to the sandbox key. Recommend run with representative seq lengths.
[06:54] [06:54] Tom: Any limits on concurrent streaming connections per key?
[07:00] Alice: Hosted has soft quotas by default; we can raise them for pilots. Concurrency scales with your usage plan; for production we recommend dedicated capacity if you need guaranteed throughput.
[07:16] Maya: When a stream times out, do we get partial content back to the client or is it lost?
[07:22] Jonas: Partial content is typically delivered — client receives chunks up to the disconnect. But if the disconnect happens before finalization, you may need to re-request with the observed partial as prefix and rely on deterministic params to continue.
[07:40] [07:40] Jonas: Live demo: I'm intentionally inducing a transient 503 to show retry behavior. Starting sequence...
[07:58] [07:58] System: event: 503 generated for this request at the edge
[08:10] Jonas: Our SDK auto-retries for safe errors. If streaming interrupted we recommend client backoff and then re-issue with idempotency key or resume token. See snippet.
[08:28] Maya: For our triage flow, we need to ensure classification labels are stable. What's the best way?
[08:34] Jonas: Use lower temp, canonical prompt, few-shot examples, and use deterministic sampling (temp 0 or top_k=1) for strict label selection. Also run evals in Redwood Optimize to track regressions.
[08:58] Maya: Speaking of Optimize — can it suggest quantization profiles for a customer workload?
[09:04] Jonas: Yes, Optimize will analyze token distribution, sequence lengths, and suggest quantization + batching configs to reduce unit cost while keeping quality. We can run a sample job on your dataset in the pilot.
[09:26] Priya: We need audit logs for requests and admin actions for 1 year.
[09:32] Alice: Enterprise plan can increase retention; logs include request metadata but not full prompts unless requested. We can produce redacted logs for compliance.
[09:50] [09:50] Maya: If we hit rate limits, what's the 429 handling pattern?
[09:55] Jonas: 429 with Retry-After header, client should honor; our SDK surfaces that. Implement retry with backoff and consider queueing at ingress, or pre-warming with reserved capacity.
[10:13] Tom: Let's talk about max_tokens — if a model truncates, do we get partial and a truncated_flag?
[10:20] Jonas: We include a flag in the response metadata indicating truncation due to max_tokens. Also console shows token usage per call to help tune max_tokens. Consider streaming early-stop tokens.
[10:40] [10:40] Maya: Any best practices for long context windows? We have multi-turn threads up to 8k tokens.
[10:46] Jonas: For long contexts use windowing, summarization + recall, or KV cache for repeated context; also choose model variant optimized for long sequences. We'll include examples.
[11:05] [11:05] Maya: Show us a retry snippet from the SDK?
[11:10] Jonas: Pasting now — node snippet with SSE: set up eventsource, on error check status, if 502/503 backoff 500ms -> 2s -> 5s, attach idempotency key.
[11:30] [11:30] System: minor crosstalk, someone drops — reconnecting
[11:45] Tom: Quick infra Q — if we need VPC peering for Private deployment later, what's involved?
[11:52] Alice: For Private you run a control plane in our managed service and can set up VPC peering or an on-prem appliance; there's a short network checklist. We'll share the runbook.
[12:10] [12:10] Maya: What about streaming parsing on our side — should we parse by punctuation or token boundaries?
[12:16] Jonas: We recommend buffer by logical tokens or newline sentinel to avoid mid-word artifacts. Use the stop tokens to force boundary.
[12:35] Priya: Can you confirm data-at-rest encryption in hosted? We require AES-256 and rotation via our KMS.
[12:42] Alice: Yes AES-256 at rest; for enterprise we support customer-managed KMS and rotation policies.
[12:58] [12:58] Jonas: Now switching to console: showing per-model cost simulation. If you drop max_tokens from 256 to 128 you can cut cost ~30% on typical prompts.
[13:20] Maya: Great. What does the sandbox key allow access to? Is it throttled?
[13:25] Jonas: Sandbox keys have elevated quotas for testing but are rate-limited to avoid abuse. We can apply your prompt set to a sandbox test harness with higher concurrency if you want.
[13:42] [13:42] System: 15-minute mark note: going to cover retry patterns then handoff
[13:58] Jonas: Important: streaming is orthogonal to model; retries should be per-request. For long-running streams consider keep-alive and heartbeat to detect stales.
[14:20] Maya: Ok timeline again — pilot by Sept end, we'd need pricing and security docs this week ideally.
[14:27] Alice: We'll send pricing and the SOC2 package today; Jonas will drop SDK snippets and the k6 harness by tomorrow.
[14:38] [14:38] Alice: Any other questions?
[14:42] Priya: One more — will you sign a DPA with our standard terms?
[14:47] Alice: Yes we have a standard DPA; legal can start review when you share the template. We'll include a draft.
[15:02] Maya: Okay thanks, useful session.
[15:06] Alice: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the pack. Next meeting: sandbox handoff + small benchmark next Tues? Does that work?
[15:12] Maya: Works for us.

Recap / Next steps:
- Send pricing + estimate (Alice)
- Share SOC2, privacy and DPA templates (Alice)
- Provide SDK streaming snippets and resume token example (Jonas)
- Provision sandbox key and k6 harness (Jonas)

End of transcript.
